## The PBB Disaster at 50

*A Conference to Commemorate & Learn from The Poisoning of Michigan*

**May 18–20, 2023 — Alma College, Alma, Michigan**

Over 200 participants gathered to mark the 50th anniversary of the 1973 PBB accident, in which Michigan Chemical Company (then owned by Velsicol) mistakenly shipped polybrominated biphenyl (PBB) flame retardant to a livestock feed mill. The resulting contamination reached roughly 8.5 million Michigan residents through the food supply — one of the largest chemical disasters in U.S. history.

### Program

**Thursday, May 18** — Opening remarks and a keynote from historian Dr. Elena Conis, author of works on chemical safety and public health.

**Friday, May 19** — Policy and community panel discussions, followed by field trips through St. Louis, the Velsicol Superfund site, and a formerly quarantined farm. The evening featured a screening of the 1977 documentary *The Poisoning of Michigan*.

**Saturday, May 20** — Sessions on philosophy, art, law, and environmental history; a PBB Heroes recognition event; and a Michigan PBB Registry community meeting.

### Funders

The conference was supported by the Michigan Humanities Council, Alma College, Emory University's Rollins School of Public Health, the Michigan PBB Registry, Central Michigan University, and the EPA.
